the membrane targeting of the voltage-gated Ca2+ channel auxiliary β2e subunits is initiated from the electrostatic insertion of its N-terminal lysine and tryptophan residues into the membrane, and that the phosphatidylinositols, phosphatidylcholines, and phosphatidylethanolamines play important roles in the membrane targeting.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of the membrane interaction of the β2 subunit of voltage-gated Ca(2+)-channels.
a molecular understanding of the mechanism by which the β2e auxiliary subunit of CaV channels interacts with the membrane.
the membrane targeting of the N-ter-minal peptide of β2e subunits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our study reveals a new mechanism of protein-lipid interaction, in which the electrostatic interaction of basic amino acid residues with negatively charged phospholipids plays a critical role.
β2e subunits are recruited to the membrane through a nonspecific electrostatic interaction between basic N-terminal residues and the anionic lipid headgroups of PS and PIP2.
the N-terminal region of β2e subunits is electrostatically recruited to the plasma membrane through the interaction of K2 and W4 residues with PS and PIP2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N-termini of β2e are electrostatically inserted into the membrane, which is stabilized through the polar interactions with PS.
the β2e N-terminus is electrostatically inserted into the membrane through the PS-β2 interaction, and that the β2 N-terminus can be a target for phospholipid regulation.
the N-termini of β2e are electrostatically inserted into the membrane, and this insertion initiates the membrane recruitment of the β2 subunit.
The main takeaway from our work is that

electrostatic interactions between the N-terminal basic residues (K2 and W5) and anionic phosphatidyl serine (PS) are critical for the membrane binding of the N- terminus of the β2 subunit of voltage-gated Ca(2+ )channels.
the β-subunit of voltage-gated Ca(2) channels is recruited to the plasma membrane through electrostatic interactions with anionic phosphol lipids.
the electrostatic insertion of the β2 subunit into the plasma membrane is a key initial step for membrane recruitment of the β2-subunit.
